package_info.why_malicious: These versions of Apache Struts (struts2-core) are blocked due to critical, well-documented security vulnerabilities that have been exploited in the wild. The policy enforces a block on all non-whitelisted versions in the 2.3.* and 2.5.* ranges to prevent the introduction of high-risk components into customer environments, reducing the attack surface for known exploits such as remote code execution.

execution_context.file_location: Nexus IQ Server policy configuration (not source code)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During dependency resolution / build-time, the policy scans all Maven dependencies and matches any artifact from org.apache.struts with an artifactId starting with struts2 and a version in the 2.3.* range, then flags the component as a policy violation, preventing its use in the build.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This policy enforces a blanket block on all 2.3.* versions of Struts2, which have a history of critical vulnerabilities, including remote code execution flaws. Such broad blocking is a strong indicator of a high-risk component.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, dependency resolution allows all versions unless a specific vulnerability is identified. Here, the policy proactively blocks an entire version range, which is only justified by severe, persistent security issues.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Blocking deprecated, unsupported, or end-of-life libraries to enforce security compliance or stability requirements.
key_indicators: Wildcard version matching (2.3.*) for a known-vulnerable component

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Coordinates do not match: maven, org.apache.struts, struts2*, 2.3.35, *, *
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During dependency resolution / build-time, the policy checks for org.apache.struts:struts2* artifacts with version 2.3.35 and exempts this specific version from the block, allowing it to pass policy enforcement and be used in the build.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This is an explicit whitelist exception for version 2.3.35, which can be risky if new vulnerabilities are discovered in this version after the policy is set. Static whitelisting can create blind spots if not regularly reviewed.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Whitelisting should be dynamic and based on up-to-date vulnerability intelligence. Hardcoded exceptions can undermine the effectiveness of broad block policies.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Allowing only security-vetted versions in highly regulated or controlled environments.
key_indicators: Exception to a broad block policy for a single version

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During dependency resolution / build-time, the policy scans all Maven dependencies and matches any artifact from org.apache.struts with an artifactId starting with struts2 and a version in the 2.5.* range, then flags the component as a policy violation, preventing its use in the build.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This policy blocks all 2.5.* versions of Struts2, indicating that even newer versions are considered untrusted until explicitly reviewed and approved. This is a sign of ongoing or unresolved security concerns.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Typically, newer versions are assumed to be safer due to security patches. Blocking all 2.5.* versions is only justified if vulnerabilities persist or if the organization requires explicit approval for each version.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Blocking untested or unstable major versions until they pass security review.

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Automated scanning of repository policy configurations should look for broad version blocks using wildcards (e.g., 2.3.*, 2.5.*) combined with explicit whitelisting of specific versions for high-risk components like org.apache.struts:struts2*. Flag policies that statically allow-list versions, as these may become outdated and introduce risk. Regularly review and update whitelists based on current vulnerability intelligence to prevent blind spots.
